summary: The gaia variant is a design + code Python implementation with both a local asyncio prototype and a SPADE-based multi-agent implementation. It addresses most functional requirements at a prototype level, including sensor data fields, periodic simulated data, aggregation, high-activity detection, and alerts to administration, pest control, and students. The SPADE implementation is not ready for use because it deserializes inter-agent message bodies with eval(), which is a critical security finding.

findings.description: The data model explicitly carries the sensor identifier, detected cockroach count, location, and timestamp required for sensor events.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:10-14 defines SensorData with sensor_id, cockroach_count, location, and timestamp.

findings.description: Cockroach detection is simulated with random counts rather than integrated with motion sensor readings, so the motion-sensor requirement is only partially satisfied.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:77-78: '# Simulate sensor data' followed by 'cockroach_count = random.randint(0, 10)'.

findings.description: The system identifies high-activity locations and forwards alerts for them.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:138 describes the threshold rule and lines 156-160 create AlertDetails for high-activity zones.

findings.description: The local asyncio implementation defines notification queues for administration, pest control, and students, but the reportable behavior is still simulated by in-process queues and print statements rather than real external notifications.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:193-198 defines alert_queue, admin_queue, pest_queue, and student_queue; lines 209-216 enqueue the same alert to each party.

findings.description: The SPADE implementation evaluates received message bodies as Python code, allowing code execution if an agent receives a malicious or malformed message body.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py:132, 228, 269, 296, and 323 call eval(msg.body) while parsing inter-agent messages.

findings.description: The implementation is duplicated across two large Python files, making behavior hard to verify and maintain.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py has 421 lines and gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py has 417 lines; both define SensorData, AlertDetails, HighActivityZone, sensor, coordinator, notification, administration, pest-control, and student components.

findings.description: The prototype relies on console prints for operational behavior instead of durable notification, logging, or integration mechanisms.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py contains 25 print() calls; examples include lines 241, 268, and 296 for administration, pest control, and student handling.

missing_requirements: Actual motion-sensor ingestion is not implemented; detections are randomly generated.
The student-facing message does not explicitly instruct affected students to improve the bad condition in their room.
logical_inconsistencies: The same system is implemented twice, once as an asyncio queue prototype and once as a SPADE agent system, with no clear statement of which implementation is authoritative.
The SPADE message protocol uses stringified dictionaries plus eval() instead of a safe, explicit message schema.
implementation_risks: Malicious or malformed SPADE messages can trigger arbitrary code execution through eval(msg.body).
Random simulated sensor values can produce false positives or false negatives if mistaken for real monitoring.
Print-based notifications do not actually contact students, administration, or a disinfection company.
Two parallel implementations can drift and make verification ambiguous.
